feedback: Written before this candidate races, so no outcome is claimed for it. The evidence is iteration 8 (score 708.5, the best raced design), iteration 9 (score 703.4, sensor y 0.08 m), and the earlier tuning history. Oval (20/20) and s-bend (20/20) complete reliably at base_speed 1.3. Slalom is still 0/20, ending off track at max_error about 0.063 m, just over the 0.06 m limit, with progress 0.56 and mean rms_error about 0.02. The robot tracks on average and loses the line at sudden alternating bends. Raising kp was already ruled out: iteration 4 at kp 3.7 hurt slalom and s-bend. The candidate changes one variable against iteration 9: base_speed 1.3 to 1.1, with the sensor geometry, kp 3.0, kd 0.8 and ki 0.02 unchanged. That is a clean test of whether more correction time per bend reduces lateral overshoot on slalom. The rationale's timing estimate (oval about 2.2 s, s-bend about 2.4 s) is inside the 3.0 s cap, but it is an estimate and not evidence. Iteration 2 at base 1.1 was never raced, so there is no measured speed-only result. The main risk is completion: if oval or s-bend drops below 20/20, or completion time approaches 2.8 s, the 500-point bonus is lost. The score cost of slower finishes is small, since the time term moves by only about 5 to 8 points. Approve so the race gives per-track telemetry for the speed effect. There is one iteration left after this one, so a second review round would cost more than it can recover. After the race, read the results in this order. (a) If the slalom still exits at max_error near 0.06 with progress no better than about 0.56, speed is not the limit, so the next step is kp about 3.3 with kd held. (b) If oval or s-bend completion falls below 20/20, or completion_time exceeds about 2.8 s, base_speed is too low, so return it to about 1.2. (c) If steering_oscillation rises above about 0.35 on any track, kd should drop toward 0.6.
requested_changes: If slalom still exits off track at max_error near 0.06 m with no progress gain over iteration 9's 0.56, leave base_speed and sensor y as they are and raise kp from 3.0 toward 3.3 with kd held at 0.8, since iteration 4 showed kp 3.7 hurt the harder tracks and a small step is safer.

If oval or s-bend completions fall below 20/20, or completion_time rises above about 2.8 s, return base_speed from 1.1 to about 1.2 with the same gains, because the 500-point completion bonus is worth far more than the small time term lost at slower speed.

If steering_oscillation rises above about 0.35 on any track at the lower speed, lower kd from 0.8 toward 0.6 with the same gains, since iteration 8 and 9 oscillation was 0.23 to 0.29 on the finishing tracks and a large rise would indicate damping, not speed, is the limit.
